lines.en: Four days had passed since Kim Dokja left.
The citadel was unchanged, without the slightest sign of impending ruin.
The sky over <Paradise>, more peaceful than ever, even languid. Looking up at that sky, Lee Gilyoung spoke in a gloomy voice.
“We've been abandoned.”
“There goes that kid again.”
“Dokja-hyung abandoned us.”
For the past two days, Lee Gilyoung had been repeating this at every opportunity, his face on the verge of tears.
Lee Jihye, who was sharpening her blade nearby, frowned.
“We finally get to take it easy. What's all the fuss about?”
“Do you know when a protagonist leaves his companions behind?”
“When his companions get in the way.”
“We've just been declared ‘useless’!”
“······What makes that man a protagonist? Honestly, Master fits the part better. And this isn't a novel, kid.”
Lee Jihye muttered her complaint, but her expression didn't look particularly bright either.
For the past four days, the group had been at peace.
It was a druglike peace. So peaceful that they wondered whether it was all right to be this peaceful.
No one threatened them, and there was nothing in the whole world for them to worry about.
They practiced their skills whenever they could and reflected on the advice Kim Dokja had left each of them.
「Gilyoung, your skills don't last long enough. If you have coins to spare, try getting ‘Patience’ or ‘Indomitable Perseverance.’ You can use the exchange or ask your sponsor.」
「Jihye, your stats are too heavily weighted toward Agility. If you have coins to spare, invest in Strength or Magic Power. Your fighting style will change depending on where you invest.」
「Yoosung, focus on raising ‘Taming’ and ‘Advanced Diverse Communication’ to their maximum levels first. If you need any other taming skills, tell me anytime.」
Was it because of what Lee Gilyoung had said?
Feeling needlessly uneasy, Lee Jihye poked Shin Yoosung, who was sitting upright beside her.
“Hey, beast kid.”
Shin Yoosung, who had been practicing [Advanced Diverse Communication] as Dokja had advised, opened her eyes at the sudden interruption.

They stuck together because they had ended up in the same group with no choice in the matter, but Shin Yoosung didn't much like Lee Jihye, who was rude to Kim Dokja. Embarrassed by her look, Lee Jihye spoke almost defensively.
“Hey, hey, don't glare at me like that. I just have something to ask.”
“What is it?”
“Do you know what Dokja-ajusshi used to do?”
Shin Yoosung's eyes widened at the unexpected question.
“You're his incarnation, so I thought you might know something. Incarnations normally learn more about their sponsors whenever their synchronization with them increases.”

In fact, whenever Lee Jihye used the Duke of Loyalty and Warfare's [stigmas], she would receive memories from Yi Sunsin's life. A stigma was, after all, the core (中核) of a Story. Learning a constellation's story whenever she used its power was inevitable.
Shin Yoosung desperately searched through the few words she knew before finally managing to speak.
“Ajusshi is······ a lonely person.”
“Hey, anyone could say that.”
“And he really loves books······.”
“Books?”
“Yes. When I think of ajusshi, things like countless pages come to mind. I'm not sure what they are······ I can't see what's written on them, either.”
After hesitating, Shin Yoosung lowered her head and continued.
“That's all I know so far. I haven't even received a stigma yet.”
“······I didn't ask to make you feel bad.”
Patting Shin Yoosung's small shoulder, Lee Jihye felt anew something she already knew. Only one person was missing, yet the atmosphere of the entire party had changed.
It struck her again how remarkable it was that they had survived this long with a lineup like this.
‘Without that man, we'd all have been fucking dead ages ago······.’
On closer inspection, every last one of them was a cause for concern.

Two kids who relied solely on Kim Dokja, a soldier who knew nothing but the manual, a beautiful young swordswoman who couldn't properly use her power because she'd ended up with the wrong sponsor······.
[The constellation ‘Maritime War God’ criticizes the patriotism of incarnation ‘Lee Jihye.’]
Lee Jihye snorted, covered her ears, and went, “Abababa.”
‘Anyway, that soldier's doing it again.’
Since the day before yesterday, Lee Hyunsung had been staring blankly into the distance, in a daze.
Knowing whom he was looking at, Lee Jihye smirked.
Perhaps having a little time to rest wasn't entirely a bad thing.
“Hey, kids.”
Watching Lee Hyunsung head somewhere, Lee Jihye suddenly spoke.
“Want to see something fun?”
For the past four days, Jung Heewon had been having nightmares.
Dreams of monsters running rampant and <Paradise> being destroyed.
When she woke, the [Sword of Judgment] Kim Dokja had left her was crying.
Hummmmm.
Reinheit had come to see her several times and asked her to serve as the citadel's guard captain. But Jung Heewon had refused.
This was the reason.
The [Sword of Judgment] cried only when ‘evil’ was nearby.
Sitting on a low slate roof, Jung Heewon surveyed <Paradise>.
Yet nowhere in the city could she see anything that looked like ‘evil.’
“Heewon-ssi, is something troubling you?”
When had he come over? Lee Hyunsung stood beside her, his face flushed.
“Oh, nothing really. It's so peaceful that I find myself thinking about all sorts of things.”
“······The same goes for me.”
Neither spoke for a while. An awkward silence settled between them.

Ever since Lee Hyunsung had saved Jung Heewon when Nirvana made her lose control a little while ago, a strange undercurrent had flowed between them. Neither of them, however, knew exactly what it was.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ disapproves of the behavior of incarnation ‘Lee Hyunsung’.]
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ warns ‘Master of Steel.’]
[The constellation ‘Master of Steel’ says this is not a matter for him to interfere in.]
Glancing down from the roof, she saw Lee Jihye and the children huddled together in hiding below.
‘······What are they doing down there?’
Just as Jung Heewon was about to call out to them, Lee Hyunsung spoke first.
“Still, I believe there must be a reason for this peace.”
“······You seem to believe Dokja-ssi had a reason for leaving us here.”
“That's the kind of person Dokja-ssi is. Finding the reason is probably up to us.”

Common sense suggested as much. But no matter how much she thought about it, she couldn't figure it out. His deliberate choice to leave them in <Paradise> suggested it had something to do with this place, but nothing on the surface told her what the problem could possibly be.
Just then, a commotion rose from the people below the roof.
“Give us back the scenarios!”
“We want to go to the ‘next floor’!”

Jung Heewon frowned. The only people full of discontent in peaceful <Paradise>. They were Paradise's protesters. They didn't even have a unifying slogan yet, but they would appear intermittently throughout <Paradise>.
Jung Heewon couldn't understand them.
Why on earth did they want to return to the ‘scenarios’?
“I think we should go down. It looks like a fight's about to break out.”
“Understood.”
But by the time Jung Heewon got down, blood was already being shed. But it wasn't a ‘fight.’ It was a one-sided beating.
Of course, the ones doing the beating were the guards, not the protesters.
Angered by their blatant use of excessive force, Jung Heewon tried to stop the guards.
“Wait! Calm down and back off! This is going too far!”
“We're carrying out our official duties. Don't interfere.”

Shaking off Jung Heewon's hand, the guard captain directed his men to gather the fallen protesters together. Small carts soon arrived, and the protesters were loaded onto them and taken away somewhere in a line.
“Catch everyone who ran away, too. Lock up everyone who was with them.”
“What should we do with that woman?”
Glancing at Jung Heewon, the guard captain shook his head.
“Leave her alone. The lord gave us orders.”
Before long, several of the protesters who had fled were also brought in.
But there were some unexpected people among them.
“I-I'm not a protester! I just happened to be passing by! Dayoung! Dayoung!”
They were the mother and daughter from Geumho Station. Jung Heewon shouted.
“Wait! She's not a protester!”
A guard replied.
“She is a protester. When we went after her, she panicked and ran. Why would she run if she hadn't done anything wrong?”
“There you have it.”
The guard captain nodded and began issuing orders again.
Jung Heewon shouted.
“No, if you suddenly chase someone, of course they'll get scared and run!”
“The charges will be established later. We don't have time. Get them moving!”
“I said wait!”
“······The lord's orders notwithstanding, if you interfere one more time, I really will arrest you.”
Absurdly enough, the word ‘arrest’ made Jung Heewon falter.
She didn't know why.
Was it because she'd suddenly returned to society after being cast into the wild for so long?
Perhaps deciding there was no stopping this now, the woman cried out.
“M-my child hasn't done anything wrong! At least let my child go!”
The guard captain briefly hesitated at the woman's scream.
After a moment's deliberation, he spoke.
“······Leave the child.”
The guards nodded and moved off with only the woman. Watching her mother being taken away, the child began to cry.
“Dayoung, listen carefully. Mommy will be back soon. All right? Stay right there and wait! Right there······!”
Her mother's voice grew more and more distant.
When Jung Heewon belatedly came to her senses and tried to follow them, several merchants who had been watching stepped in.
“Miss, don't do anything foolish. It's no use. That's the law of <Paradise>.”
“······Where are they going?”
“Paradise's underground prison, I suppose.”
“Underground prison?”
“No one's allowed in except the guards. Whatever they did, no one who's gone in there has ever come back. Tsk, tsk······ I feel sorry for the kid, but her mother should've obeyed the law.”
The merchants dispersed, responding indifferently as though it were nothing out of the ordinary.
Jung Heewon stood dazed for a moment, then approached the crying child. Hesitating over what to do, she carefully took the crying child's hand.
The moment that warmth curled into her hand, something suddenly surged up inside her.
······<Paradise>?
“I think we know what we need to do.”
She turned to find Lee Jihye and the others standing there.
They all looked as though they had found their own ‘scenario.’
Lee Hyunsung spoke.
“This looks like it could turn into something big. I'm not sure we can manage it on our own.”
“Dokja-ajusshi must've left because he trusted us. He's probably handling something much bigger himself. He always does.”
“That's right. Hyung must be fighting monsters all by himself again, with that serious look on his face.”
There was no way Kim Dokja would simply leave without a reason.

Whether it was to protect his companions from an approaching threat or to clear this scenario······ whatever the reason, Kim Dokja was surely grappling desperately with his own life even at this very moment.
At last, Jung Heewon spoke.
“Let's do this ourselves this time.”
They couldn't rely solely on Kim Dokja every time.
Surely, somewhere out of sight, Kim Dokja was carrying out another hellish scenario.
“Hey! This is fucking sweet, Kim Dokja. Why didn't you start living like this ages ago?”
A sports car raced across the vast <Abyss Plains>, its engine roaring with terrifying force.
“······Good question.”

Over the past four days, we had cleared no fewer than three ‘hidden scenarios’ concealed in the <Abyss Plains>. Clearing them hadn't been difficult. Unlike everything we'd done so far, I had freely used my knowledge of the future.
“That one's weakness appears in the 34th round. So, if you press the three little spots on its lower back······.”
“That one's area attack is dangerous. But it leaves an opening after using it······.”
“That boss's weak point is its anus······.”
Traveling with Han Sooyoung also made things easier in some ways.
“Okay, the anus, got it.”
I didn't have to explain why I knew these things, and Han Sooyoung didn't question anything I told her.
As a result, we had acquired two Star Relics. The remaining item was SSS-grade, but as long as we were on these plains, it was just as useful as a Star Relic.
[SSS-Class Ferrarghini]
This car was part of an SSS-grade series made by the [Mass Production Maker].
Vrooooom!

Not only could it go as fast as [Way of the Wind] without using Magic Power, but its front and rear [SSS-Grade Magic Power Turrets] were also useful for annihilating large numbers of enemies. Thanks to that, we were racing across the plains, thoroughly enjoying the feeling of being out for a drive for once.
What should I call this?
The ‘Deluxe Regressor Package,’ perhaps?
I found myself resenting that bastard Yoo Joonghyuk all over again.
He must have been enjoying luxuries like this while I worked myself to death clearing scenarios.
Even more excited than I was, Han Sooyoung had been standing up in the passenger seat, throwing both arms into the air and shouting nonstop.
“I'll never be a sucker again! I'll live selfishly, for myself alone!”
That textbook regressor mindset made me want to retort, “You've always lived only for yourself.”
[A considerable number of constellations are pleased with the spirited declaration by incarnation ‘Han Sooyoung’.]
[A considerable number of constellations approve of your approach.]
[You have acquired 20000 coins.]
Ratatatatat!
Monsters approaching from the distance burst apart under the Ferrarghini's magic bullets.
Exhilarated by raking in coins, Han Sooyoung thrust her small chest toward the sky and shouted at me.
“Kim Dokja! You say something too! When will you get another chance to feel like this?”
At her words, I hesitated for a moment.
It felt embarrassing somehow, but part of me agreed with Han Sooyoung.
Come to think of it, my life had never gone this well.
A life of endless overtime.
I'd taken public transportation because I couldn't even afford a used car, let alone a Ferrari.
So······ wasn't I allowed to enjoy myself a little?
After hesitating, I squeezed my eyes shut and shouted in a timid voice.
“I-I'm the protagonist!”
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ covers her eyes in embarrassment.]
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ considers switching channels.]
[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ is intoxicated by your eighth-grade edginess.]
Fuck······ Can't I enjoy myself a little?
Anyway······ things should be starting to happen in <Paradise> around now.
There was the course of the original novel to go by, and my companions would probably handle it well.
I couldn't remember the last time things had gone this smoothly.
At this rate, we'd clear the scenario in no time······.
[A great fate desires your death.]
For a moment, I wondered if I'd misheard and even dug around in my ear.
But the message didn't change.
[A great fate desires your death.]
What was this?
Bewildered, I slammed on the brakes.
Han Sooyoung let out a small scream as the sudden stop threw her forward.
“······What the hell? I was just getting into it!”
“Be quiet for a second.”
I listened again. This time, the message appeared on a screen as well as sounding aloud.
[A great fate desires your death.]
That made three times.
I swallowed without realizing it.
Damn it. Had a ‘fate message’ ever sounded three times in the original novel?
I thought back.
Probably······ Yoo Joonghyuk in the 71st round.
Back then, Yoo Joonghyuk's name had been entered in King Yama's death register.
Damn it, what was about to happen?
Han Sooyoung pressed me for an answer.
“Why? What's going on?”
“Someone has read my ‘fate.’”
Fate. In Ways of Survival, it was a word as frightening as ‘probability.’
Strictly speaking, this too was a power that used ‘probability’ in the broader sense. But there was a reason it was given a separate name.
‘Fate’ was a power constellations exercised by using their accumulated probability cost.
“Uh, hold on. I feel like I've heard about that too······.”
“It was probably mentioned briefly near the beginning of the original novel.”
“Fate······ Isn't it something like ‘Future Sight’?”
“There are similarities, but it's a little different.”
In fact, it was very different.
Reading fate wasn't simply reading ‘information about the future.’
In some ways, it was far more dangerous.
“If ‘Future Sight’ merely lets you glimpse a predictable future, ‘fate’ is a ‘power’ that forces a predictable future to happen.”
Unable to tell whether Han Sooyoung understood, I added an explanation.
“Say I step on the accelerator five seconds from now. If you looked with ‘Future Sight,’ you'd see me driving, right?”
“······Well, sure.”
“But if I knew that future, I could find some way to avoid stepping on the accelerator.”
“I guess you could.”

“But ‘fate’ is different. If someone reads the fate ‘Kim Dokja steps on the accelerator five seconds from now,’ it creates a ‘compulsion’ that persists until that fate is withdrawn or fulfilled. So, to put it simply······.”
“You're guaranteed to step on the accelerator.”
When I nodded, Han Sooyoung spoke as though something didn't add up.
“But that's a little strange.”
“What is?”
“It doesn't square with probability. From what you're saying, ‘fate’ is powerful enough to interfere with a scenario. Who the hell can force something like that to happen?”
“······Who do you think?”
In principle, this scenario had no dokkaebi interference.
That left only one group of bastards who could interfere.
Understanding immediately, Han Sooyoung replied.
“Even a constellation couldn't do that alone······.”
“The problem is, they're not alone.”
“What?”
“Only great nebulae can read ‘fate.’”
No sooner had I spoken than an explosive roar erupted ahead.
Rrrrrrumble!
Something was approaching at a terrifying speed.
A being on an entirely different level from the pathetic monsters we'd faced so far.
Han Sooyoung's face went pale.
“······Kim Dokja, what exactly did that fate message you got say?”
“That I'm going to die.”
“Damn it, you should've said that first! I knew things were going a little too well······.”
Just as Han Sooyoung began spewing curses and tried to get out of the car.
A figure appeared in the billowing smoke ahead.
I reflexively drew [Unbreakable Faith], but the man spoke first.
“Kim Dokja. I have something to tell you.”
I'd never seen this man before.
But the aura emanating from his entire body was familiar.
Instinctively, I felt he wasn't an enemy.
The moment I caught the fragrant scent of wine and the air of excessive excitement, I had an inkling of whose incarnation he was.
“······Did you come to tell me I'm going to die?”
Reeking of drunkenness, Dionysus's incarnation smiled at me with the whites of his eyes showing.
“Oh, you knew?”

I still had a favorable impression of Dionysus. On my way to the banquet hall, he'd once descended in his true body and fought for me. But in a situation like this, things were different. I spoke warily.
“Were you the ones who read my fate?”
“Yes. It was <Olympus> that read your fate. But if you're asking whether I was one of them, the answer is no.”
“What does that mean?”
Dionysus's incarnation merely smiled.
The moment I saw that smile, a thought flashed through my mind.
“Could <Olympus> have split?”
“Clever as always.”
······Already?
This too was happening earlier than in the original novel.
The rift within <Olympus> had been expected, but it wasn't supposed to happen until after scenario 10 ended, at the earliest.
“It's not just <Olympus>. There are constellations after you. Very mighty, very powerful ones.”
I'd expected as much.
Otherwise, there was no way something like ‘fate’ would be making itself felt.
“Why are they after me?”
“Those powerful bastards are bigger cowards than you'd think. They're afraid of your influence.”
“But aren't I just a fledgling constellation?”

“Normally, yes. But this scenario that began on Earth is very special. Some constellations believe it's the very scenario we've been waiting for all this time. Ah, don't make that face. I didn't say that expecting you to understand.”
I wanted to tell him this was just how my face normally looked, but Dionysus continued without pausing.
“Anyway, all you need to know is that this scenario is incredibly important to us. And you just had to turn up in that particular scenario.”
“I don't know what this is about, but you're saying I'm in the way.”

“Yes. You can't help being in the way. Probability affects you far less than it does other constellations. You even have overwhelming strength and growth potential compared with other incarnations. That's why some nebulae believe they must bring you into their fold, or eliminate you if they can't.”
I looked at Dionysus for a moment.
“······Why are you telling me this?”
That was what I most wanted to know.
Why was Dionysus showing me such kindness?
“Because I like your story, of course.”
Dionysus gave a hearty laugh and added,
“A few other constellations and I believe you are someone who can reach ■■.”

Jung Heewon and her companions spent the entire day investigating Paradise's ‘underground prison.’ Since there was no way for a large group to enter all at once, they decided to split up and each find a way in. The method Jung Heewon chose was, in its own way, a direct approach.
‘Blend in and go inside.’

New criminals appeared in the afternoon, and, having received a [Recluse’s Cloak] from Uriel, she followed the guards when the ‘underground prison’ opened. Unaware of her presence, the guards and their bound prisoners opened the door leading underground.
The prison was far deeper than she'd expected, and the darkness of the underground passage was darker than she'd imagined.
‘······How far down are we going?’
The depth made no sense.
Even for a prison, was it necessary to hold people this far underground? Surely this would make transporting them inconvenient too······.
Just as the question arose, the guards all stopped in their tracks.
Strangely, tension showed on every one of their faces.
“Take them only as far as that spot! Then we pull out immediately!”

The guards were frightened, as though they'd set foot somewhere they shouldn't. Even the intimidating guard captain was afraid. Soon, a thick iron door appeared. When it opened, it revealed an entrance secured with iron bars. Layer upon layer of bars. The prison was excessively fortified for a place built to confine humans.
“Everyone inside!”
Herding the prisoners inside as though tossing in luggage, the guards quickly hurried back toward the surface.
“U-uaaagh!”
“Please save us!”
Having slipped inside among the prisoners, Jung Heewon gave a low groan as she watched them struggle frantically.
Why on earth had these people been thrown in here?
What was happening in this place?
“U-ugh······ Where the hell are we?”
The prisoners staggered about, looking around.
Dim lamps were lit, but their surroundings were very dark. Without her [Night Vision] skill, even Jung Heewon would have lost her way in the darkness long ago.
‘This is a prison?’
No matter how much she looked around, it didn't feel like a ‘prison.’ The surroundings were more like a natural cave, and she couldn't see any cells separating the prisoners.
No, she couldn't see any prisoners already confined here at all.
‘How do they distribute food? What is this place?’
The utterly incomprehensible workings of this ‘underground prison.’
The prisoners who'd come in with her seemed equally bewildered.
“What are we supposed to do here by ourselves?”
“Hello! Is anyone there?”
The frightened prisoners shouted, but no answer came.
Instead, a faint sound like a cry came from beyond the darkness.
Grrrrrr.
Jung Heewon slowly drew the [Sword of Judgment].
Hummmmm.
Ever since she'd set foot here, the sword had been howling more fiercely.
‘This is······.’
The moment an eerie sensation brushed the back of her neck, Jung Heewon shouted sharply.
“Everyone, run!”
But it was already too late. Monsters had shot out of the darkness and pounced on the people.
“A-aaaaaagh!”
“Help! Aaaaaagh!”
Strange leopardlike creatures were savagely biting and tearing at people's arms and legs. Limbs torn away like pieces of toys flew into the air with spurts of blood.

Her original plan had been to stay hidden, rescue only the woman from Geumho Station, and leave. But this changed things. As [Demon Slaying], which had nearly reached level 10, unleashed its ghostly energy, a crimson aura wrapped around her entire body.
Shhhrak!

[Kendo] traced a perfect line. Along that clean segment, the leopards' bodies split like sheets of paper. More of the agitated leopards lunged at her, but she dispatched the charging beasts cleanly with a succession of sword strikes.
Here, amid swarms of demons, Jung Heewon's power was truly at its peak.
“I-I don't know who you are, but thank y······.”
Groping through the darkness, the people searched for signs of her presence and offered their thanks.
But Jung Heewon was in no state of mind to accept their thanks.
She was examining the faces of the fallen leopards.
‘What the hell is this?’
The leopards had human faces.
Reflexively rising to her feet, Jung Heewon ran into the darkness.
A terror that chilled every one of her senses.
After running for a long time, she came upon a cavern so vast that she couldn't begin to gauge its size. Strictly speaking, it wasn't an empty cavern. Countless monsters filled it.
Grrrr······.
Gwaaaaaah!
Was this what a demonic realm (魔境) in the human world would look like?
Not just grade-5 species, but grade-4 and grade-3 species. And others whose grades she couldn't even identify.
“This is <Paradise>······.”
She couldn't find the woman from Geumho Station.
Of course she wouldn't be able to find her.
She must have already been eaten by these creatures, or······.
Gaaaaaah!
Become one of them.

Sensing a living presence, the monsters grew excited. Most were hybrids of demons and other monster species. Some had the forms of insect king species, others of non-human species······ There were even creatures whose shapes resembled ones she'd seen outside.
She saw the prisoners approaching from behind.
“Don't come here!”

But before her shout could reach them, the ground shook and the monsters' feast began. Monsters poured out of passages branching from the cavern like tunnels in an anthill. Biting her lip, Jung Heewon activated [Hell Flames Ignition].
‘I shouldn't have come alone.’
No, what could they have done even if they'd come together?
Even if Lee Hyunsung or the children had been with her.
Could they have fought these overwhelming enemies?
Perhaps it was fortunate that she'd come alone.
“Aaaaaaaaagh!”

As the criminals were mercilessly reduced to prey, Jung Heewon swung the [Sword of Judgment], imbued with [Hell Flames Ignition]. The burning archangel's fiery heat filled the cavern, and the startled demons briefly retreated with cries of alarm.
But she had no idea how long this standoff would last.
Just as some of the monsters watching the flames were about to boldly leap forward.
“You've come, incarnation of the archangel.”
At that voice, the monsters that hadn't feared even the flames backed away with faint whimpers.
She turned to find Reinheit, the lord of Paradise, standing there.
“Have you decided to become my guard captain now?”
“······You can say that after seeing this?”
Jung Heewon ground her teeth as she spoke.
“You're a liar. Paradise? A place free from the terror of the scenarios? You built this shit and still dare to say that?”
She pointed the [Sword of Judgment] at Reinheit.
Kim Dokja had been right.
There was no such thing as <Paradise> in this world.
We······ have no choice but to continue the scenarios.
“If you wish to kill me, you may.”
“I'll do it with or without your permission.”
Of course she would.
She would end this horrific nightmare, even if she had to borrow her sponsor's power.
[Activating ‘Hour of Judgement’!]
[The constellations of Absolute Good agonize over your request.]
Jung Heewon was startled by the message.
······Agonize?
Anyone could see that Reinheit was evil.
This man was deceiving countless incarnations and mass-producing monsters underground.
How could he possibly not be evil?
[The constellations of Absolute Good leave the judgment to incarnation ‘Jung Heewon.’]
Reinheit spoke.
“If you kill me, <Paradise> will end.”
At those words, Jung Heewon's blazing [Hell Flames Ignition] briefly diminished.
Wearing a faint smile, Reinheit continued.
“Jung Heewon-ssi, hadn't you actually suspected that this place existed?”
“Deep down, you must have known. That there is no perfect <Paradise>. The obvious truth that wherever there is beauty, there must also be a shadow.”
Jung Heewon couldn't answer.
To claim she hadn't known would be dishonest.
Of course she'd considered it too. That this place might also be hiding some horrific truth.
Though she hadn't imagined it would take this form······.
“······What are you planning to do with all these mass-produced monsters? Conquer the [Dark Castle]?”
“Nothing at all. They are merely nourishment for <Paradise>.”
An enormous tree trunk stood in the center of the cavern.
Branches extended like tentacles, probing the monsters around them.
Jung Heewon realized where those woody stems led.
The little flower blooming on the hill, Perpetual Motion.
Her legs began to tremble without her realizing it.
Surely this tree wasn't······.
“Don't you find it strange? Why do the countless demons swarming the [Dark Castle] leave this place alone?”
She had thought it strange.
There were too many shortcomings to call this <Paradise> a natural fortress.
“Why so many [demons] have appeared in the [Dark Castle].”

The swiftly moving stems snatched up the nearby humans one by one. The prisoners screamed, but had no time to resist. Moving at tremendous speed, the stems bound their bodies tightly and tossed them into a hole in the trunk.
Fssssss!

A horrific noise sounded, and screams rang out as though souls were being torn from living beings. Then, a little later, a bud opened on one of the tree's stems. Jung Heewon trembled, instinctively knowing what would be born from it.
Before even a few minutes had passed, a strange creature emerged from the bud. It was the human the tree had just swallowed.
Kraaaaaaaaah!
Perpetual Motion was a tree that made demons.
Jung Heewon shuddered.
